summary: Before upgrading 2.4 to 2.6, replace encrypted SAML SP private keys with unencrypted keys, since 2.6 authenticators don't support encrypted keys and the authenticator otherwise isn't migrated; also maps SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ENABLED_IDPS and SP settings to gateway IDP_URL, IDP_X509_CERT, IDP_ENTITY_ID, SP_ENTITY_ID, SP_PRIVATE_KEY.
questions: Why was my SAML authenticator not migrated to platform gateway?
Does AAP 2.6 support encrypted SAML private keys?
How do SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ENABLED_IDPS settings map to gateway?
SSO users can't log in after upgrading to 2.6 with SAML

answer_card.title: SAML authenticator migration
answer_card.answer_md:
- AAP 2.6 authenticators **do not support encrypted private keys**.
- Before upgrading from 2.4, replace an encrypted `SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_SP_PRIVATE_KEY` with an **unencrypted** key.
- If you skip this, the SAML authenticator isn't migrated; a local admin must recreate it, delaying SSO logins.
- Settings map to gateway keys: `IDP_URL`, `IDP_ENTITY_ID`, `IDP_X509_CERT`, `IDP_ATTR_USERNAME`, `IDP_ATTR_EMAIL`, `SP_ENTITY_ID`, `SP_PUBLIC_CERT`, `SP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
